name: dignified
quote: My boss handled the layoffs as professionally as possible.
description: Admiration for someone's behavior perceived as calm, graceful, and patient in a challenging situation.
perceptions: That person is treating this situation as appropriately serious.
I admire their calm, mature, patient reaction.
personOfInterestExperiences: desire to be perceived a certain way

guidance.description: Some individuals grow up with a strong sense of dignity, while others may develop it over time as an adult. Building it may begin with healing from your past and committing to a better future that you can be proud of. It can also look like learning more about yourself and staying true to your boundaries and morals.

comparisons.description: Seeing someone else as being 'dignified' is a specific type of admiration. Specifically, you approve of their calm, mature, patient, serious behavior in a challenging situation.
Someone can view a task as being important but not handle it with calm and mature dignity. They may respond to setbacks with frustration or even undignified and inappropriate outbursts.

variations.name: inherent dignity
variations.description: A pattern of social interaction that strives to treat every human being as having worth.
perceptions: Everyone deserves to be treated fairly by the law.
Everyone deserves the chance to improve themselves.

comparisons.description: The idea behind 'inherent dignity' is to give people room to improve their self-regard, so perhaps be more likely to act consistently in a dignified way.

guidance.description: Promoting human dignity is an active endeavor that requires intentionality and commitment. Here are several practical ways to support and uphold human dignity in our everyday lives.

commentaries.quote: Dignity consists not in possessing honors, but in the consciousness that we deserve them.
Self-respect is the root of discipline: The sense of dignity grows with the ability to say no to oneself.

Dignity is as essential to human life as water, food, and oxygen. The stubborn retention of it, even in the face of extreme physical hardship, can hold a man's soul in his body long past the point at which the body should have surrendered it.
Politeness is a sign of dignity, not subservience.

'Dignity' is used in two rather different ways. The first is 'earned dignity' -- the admiration of someone that is expressing a healthy self-regard. The second is 'human dignity' -- the principle of treating others as if they had healthy self-regard in the hopes this encourages them to live up to it.
